source: https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nim/nvidia/models/audio2emotion_model (workbook ID 125, read in Chrome 2026-10-16; Overview page plus Model Card++ pages bias, explainability, privacy, safety-and-security; raw/ngc_nim_nvidia_audio2emotion_model.md). Replaces ngc-peoplenet, for which the hosted model returned HTTP 400.

modelDetails.type: Speech emotion recognition classifier for six emotions: anger, disgust, fear, joy, neutral and sadness
modelDetails.architecture: Transformer, Wav2Vec2 (developed from Wav2Vec2-Large-LV60), 3.1 x 10^8 parameters
modelDetails.description: Audio2Emotion is a speech emotion recognition model embedded in the Audio2Face-3D microservice; it is ready for commercial and non-commercial use.
modelDetails.license: License Agreement for NVIDIA Audio2Emotion Model for Use with Audio2Face Project

intendedUse.primaryIntendedUseCases: Converting speech audio into emotional states that drive realistic 3D facial animations within the NVIDIA Audio2Face project
intendedUse.primaryIntendedUsers: Audio2Face developers, speech analysis researchers, human-computer interaction developers, affective computing researchers
intendedUse.primaryIntendedDomain: Speech emotion recognition, audio analysis, human-computer interaction and Audio2Face integration

factors.hardware: NVIDIA GPUs (Ampere, Blackwell, Hopper, Lovelace, Pascal and Turing architectures) on Linux; inference with TensorRT

evaluation.performance: Accuracy (Top-1) of 80% or more on clean audio
evaluation.metrics: Accuracy (Top-1), throughput and latency, emotion classification confidence scores

trainingData.dataset: 30029 audio samples from internal datasets, RAVDESS, CREMA-D, JL Corpus, EMO-DB, Emozionalmente and TTS GPT 4o, labelled by humans

modelCardContent.caveatsAndRecommendations: Integration into AI systems requires additional testing with use-case-specific data before deployment; Developers should work with their internal model team to ensure the model meets the requirements of the relevant industry and use case and addresses unforeseen product misuse

ethicalConsiderations.typeOfBias: Age, gender, linguistic background, accent, speech patterns and cultural context were considered for participation of adversely impacted groups
ethicalConsiderations.biasMitigation: Training data includes diverse speakers across multiple datasets (RAVDESS, CREMA-D, JL, Lindy & Rodney, EMO-DB, Emozionalmente, TTS GPT 4o) to reduce demographic bias
ethicalConsiderations.privacyConcerns: Audio recordings containing human speech and emotional expressions were used to create the model; the output is emotion classification probabilities from audio input
ethicalConsiderations.safetyMeasures: The principle of least privilege limits access for dataset generation and model development; Dataset access is restricted during training and dataset license constraints are adhered to
ethicalConsiderations.riskFactors: The model may misclassify emotions in edge cases
ethicalConsiderations.prohibitedDomains: Use outside the NVIDIA Audio2Face project; Use for the purpose of emotion recognition; Standalone emotion recognition applications or general-purpose audio analysis
ethicalConsiderations.regulatoryAdherence: Consent was obtained for personal data used; A mechanism honors data subject rights of access and deletion; Personal data was minimized to what was required; Data labeling complies with privacy laws
ethicalConsiderations.limitations: Requires clear audio input at a 16 kHz sampling rate; may struggle with overlapping speech or very noisy environments
